title.narrative: By 2029, a responsive and enabling policy environment is in place that upholds children’s and young people’s rights to a clean, safe, and healthy environment in their schools and communities.

% of CSOs that demonstrate improved organizational capacity across core areas (e.g., governance, resource mobilization, procurement, learning systems) using a standardised capacity self-assessment tool (OCA). (STRENGTHENING 1.1)

% of children, youth, and community members engaged in at least one environmental/climate advocacy action annually, disaggregated by gender, age, disability, and conflict-affected status. (ENGAGE 3.1)

% of targeted households or community groups adopting at least one new preparedness measure, adaptation practice, or climate-smart livelihood as a result of project support (e.g., drought-tolerant crops, rainwater harvesting, reforestation, climate smart agriculture, solar power adoption etc.) (disaggregated) (PREPARE 4.2)
By 2029, children and young people demonstrate improved knowledge and are actively engaged as environmental stewardship actors and advocates in their schools and communities.

% of climate education and leadership initiatives (school and community) that achieve inclusive participation, with equitable representation of women, girls, and other under-represented groups in content, leadership roles, and membership. (INFORM 2.2)

% of targeted children, youth, teachers, community members, and duty bearers who complete climate, biodiversity, and environmental sustainability training and demonstrate improved knowledge and to take informed climate action (disaggregated, gender, age, and disability) (Inform 2.1).

% of targeted community members (children, youth, and adults) who demonstrate improved preparedness and capacity to respond to climate-related shocks and stresses (disaggregated by gender, age, disability) (PREPARE 4.1.)
